root_cause.text: In powerpc kexec’s `wake_offline_cpus()` path, the code tried to online all present CPUs without first restoring SMT to an enabled/full-thread state, so `cpu_bootable()` rejected secondary or disallowed SMT threads and `add_cpu()` failed during kexec reboot preparation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `kexec_smt_reenable()` before the CPU-wakeup loop and explicitly states that `add_cpu()` can fail because `cpu_bootable()` returns false for CPUs failing `cpu_smt_thread_allowed()` or for non-primary threads when SMT is disabled; it then fixes this by setting `cpu_smt_num_threads = threads_per_core` and `cpu_smt_control = CPU_SMT_ENABLED` before waking offline CPUs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Re-enable SMT during kexec CPU setup so offline CPUs can be brought online successfully.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function `kexec_smt_reenable()` was added. Under `CONFIG_SMP` and `CONFIG_HOTPLUG_SMT`, it takes the device hotplug lock, sets `cpu_smt_num_threads` to `threads_per_core`, sets `cpu_smt_control` to `CPU_SMT_ENABLED`, and then releases the lock. A comment was added explaining that `wake_offline_cpus()` can fail because `cpu_bootable()` rejects CPUs when SMT is disabled or secondary SMT threads are not allowed.
intent_record.how: This change re-enables SMT state before kexec-related CPU bring-up so that offline CPUs, including SMT sibling threads, become bootable again and `add_cpu()` in `wake_offline_cpus()` can succeed. It prevents kexec preparation from being blocked by SMT-disabled bootability checks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Re-enable SMT before waking offline CPUs during kexec CPU bring-up.
intent_record.what: A call to `kexec_smt_reenable();` was inserted at the start of `wake_offline_cpus()`, before the loop that iterates over present CPUs and wakes any offline ones.
intent_record.how: When this function runs, SMT is re-enabled before attempting to bring offline CPUs back online, ensuring the system restores SMT state as part of the kexec CPU wakeup path.
